lessonAssessments.conclusion: The alphabet-first placement agrees with the book. App checks chiefly recognize printed identities and case pairs; they do not establish word decoding or sign reading. The newly added name inventory is compatible with the book's early supplementary name material, but does not resolve the missing foundation modalities.
lessonAssessments.scope: Section locators, introductory English prose and visual page-1 verification; full letter/sound correspondence and sign exercises NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Handwriting and pronunciation belong here in the book. The app explicitly delegates them to the owned copy and repeats Unit 1 print checks. That is an honest limitation, but it leaves the required additional app foundation practice incomplete.
lessonAssessments.scope: Heading spine and sampled stress discussion; handwritten letter recognition, all phonetic examples and pronunciation performance NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Phrases, naming and gender occupy the expected lesson. Current gender instruction distinguishes masculine nouns with first-declension behavior. Narrow phrase and gender recognition can support this lesson; conversational transfer and the full basic-grammar scope have not been demonstrated.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled gender explanation; full dialogues, exercises and exceptions NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Pronouns, present conjugation, stress and introductory cases are sequenced consistently. New subject-role checks address the earlier translation-only nominative problem. They establish a bounded recognition task rather than general productive command of present tense or cases.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled pronoun/conjugation prose; every paradigm, stress value and case exercise NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Question words, prepositional examples and indeclinable nouns match the lesson's topic order. The old database-flag framing has been replaced with ordinary noun-behavior language. Written recognition does not verify the spoken question intonation described in the book.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled question-intonation explanation; full prepositional exceptions and spoken execution NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Possessives, accusative functions, direction and names are in their expected position. Current animacy checks include a complete inanimate-object clause, and object-form prompts now specify the target. Coverage of the book's naming/register distinctions remains only partially inspected.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled animacy discussion; complete names, etiquette and dialogue coverage NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Adjective agreement, demonstratives, case forms and adverbs match the lesson. The current packet contains the previously missing worked agreement contrasts and fuller repair. This supports the bounded supplied forms; it does not establish every adjective declension or productive agreement context. Required adverb-invariance checks still measure source wording/location rather than invariance (CC011).
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings, sampled agreement prose and targeted app teaching; full adjective paradigms and adverb coverage NOT_VERIFIED. Newly visually read PDF85–87/printed73–75: accusative modifier forms, prepositional note and adverb section. General paradigms remain incomplete.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Plural formation, spelling and existence language fit the book sequence. The same printed noun question is used in guided spelling work and an independent plural check, reducing the latter's evidence of transfer. Buying-things use remains broader than the inspected recognition tasks. Analyzed genitive absence in current Unit8 is earlier than the book/authority introduction (CC012); positive existence is the supported Unit8 scope.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled plural explanation; full irregular inventory and shopping dialogue NOT_VERIFIED. Complete existence §8.9 and next-section boundary visually read on PDF97–98/printed85–86.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Number ranges and counted-noun patterns fit the introduction of the genitive. The packet distinguishes one/two agreement and quantity patterns. Broad genitive singular/plural formation and money use require more than selecting retained number or rule lines.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled genitive introduction; all number forms, exceptions and money applications NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Possession, absence and expanded genitive functions are placed consistently. Current absence explanations are complete, unlike the old cut-off options. One absence question is identical across a guided task and a purported independent possession check, leaving a residual independence defect.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled absence explanation; complete genitive functions, adjective paradigms and dialogues NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Past forms and reflexive verbs match the book's first-introduction boundary. The former aspect-labelled objective now tests past gender agreement, avoiding analyzed aspect instruction before Unit 12. Irregular forms, negative stress and reflexive interpretation remain only partially assessed.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled past/existence prose; all irregulars, reflexive functions and stress cases NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Future/aspect introduction, dative and prepositional plural follow the book. Current wording correctly treats aspect pairing as bounded and context dependent. Pair recognition does not establish choosing aspect, all dative uses or sentence production.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled aspect introduction; complete dative/spelling paradigms and future applications NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Past aspect, infinitive choice and reported speech are placed consistently. The revised caution against mechanically converting English tense into Russian aspect is appropriate. Supplied report-frame choices offer narrower evidence than selecting aspect and tense in unfamiliar discourse.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled past-aspect prose; all infinitive/reported-speech applications NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Future aspect and impersonal constructions match the lesson. The dative experiencer belongs to this scope, supporting its removal as an analyzed Unit 7 topic. Current checks remain a bounded selection task rather than evidence of independent future-aspect or impersonal sentence formation.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled impersonal explanation; complete future-context and dialogue coverage NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Imperative forms are correctly located. The book also applies aspect to requests, repetition and prohibitions; the app's consolidation checks only identify partners in two verb pairs. Knowing those partners does not demonstrate choosing an imperative aspect for a communicative context.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled imperative/aspect rules; all irregular imperative forms and dialogues NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Instrumental nouns, modifiers and complements belong here. The required schedule also names surname declension, and the book treats it separately. No dedicated surname teaching/check chain appears among the packet's objectives; the book assignment must not be read as demonstrated app coverage of that topic.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled instrumental/surname explanation; every surname paradigm and instrumental application NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Time, ordinals, dates, years and age are in the expected lesson. The current packet has distinct clock-question and book-selection checks alongside quarter/half and calendar tasks. This resolves the old repeated clock-vocabulary route, while leaving full productive clock/date use unverified.
lessonAssessments.scope: New English explanatory prose read on PDF213–224/printed201–212. Native examples visually inspected on PDF214,217,219,221/printed202,205,207,209. Remaining native paradigms, full exercise/dialogue sets and later passage NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Comparison, superlatives and relative clauses match the lesson. Six packet items recognize selected forms and meanings, including a prepositional relative. That is a useful subset, but it does not establish the full comparative formation or relative-case selection scope.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled comparison formation prose; every irregular comparison and relative-case application NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Conditional, obligation and prefixes occupy the expected place. Current wording distinguishes speaker agreement from a whole-sentence gloss and warns against automatic prefix pairing. Broad conditional use and prefix semantics exceed the inspected recognition evidence.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled conditional introduction; full prefix inventory and dialogue NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: The added independent directionality contexts address the former label-only gap. The book also distinguishes kinds of bringing and links prefixed motion with aspect; the app's inspected checks concentrate on means, setting out, paths and directionality. Full bringing coverage is not established by an unprefixed carry/lead/transport gloss.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled directionality/aspect/bringing prose; all motion pairs and path uses NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Own-possession and reflexive reference are in the correct lesson. The book's purpose scope includes clause constructions, while the app's guided purpose item recognizes one conjunction and its two independent items recognize condition and cause instead. Neither independent item demonstrates the purpose construction taught here.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled purpose/control-construction prose; complete possession cases and clause applications NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Number declension, both, one-and-a-half and collectives are correctly placed. The book separately treats general fractions and numeral-subject agreement. One-and-a-half phrase recognition is narrower than those topics, so the required fractions scope is not fully evidenced by the current objective set.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled numeral agreement/fraction prose; complete declension tables and general fraction applications NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: When, duration and completion-time expressions match the lesson. The app now has a bounded completion-over-time contrast and no longer describes it as wholly absent. It remains narrower than every time clause or aspect interaction in the book. Three current guided/independent time-expression task pairs repeat the same substantive question (CC010).
lessonAssessments.scope: New explanatory prose read on PDF295–300/printed283–288; native constructions visually inspected on PDF297,299,300/printed285,287,288. Remaining native examples, full exercises, dialogue and later material NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Negation, case variation and placement align with the book. Current wording correctly separates indefinite reference from negative absence, and warns that word order alone does not fix every interpretation. The bounded contextual contrast is appropriate evidence only for its stated readings. One concord guided/independent pair repeats the same substantive task (CC010).
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled negation/scope explanation; full case-choice exceptions and all negative paradigms NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Names and politeness fit the lesson. The app cautiously distinguishes polite/plural address and documented name forms. Its name-centered diminutive practice is narrower than the book's treatment of other diminutive morphology; broad diminutive competence cannot be inferred.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled name/diminutive discussion; complete diminutive formation and register conventions NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Indefinite reference, word order and correspondence follow the book. The app separates postal components, letter framework and recipient/register cautions. These bounded tasks should not be presented as complete postal or pragmatic writing competence.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled address discussion; all indefinite contrasts, information structure and letter texts NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Passive participle interpretation and stress occupy the expected lesson. The book explicitly treats present passive as extra, supporting the app's optional boundary. Required past-passive stress and comprehension are distinct tasks; two marked forms do not establish a general stress rule.
lessonAssessments.scope: Section spine and sampled present-passive qualification; complete formation, exceptions and stress paradigms NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Current relative-time and shared-subject interpretations agree with the sampled book explanation. Authentic guided clauses now differ from independent research-cue sentences. The two independent cue families still need separate retained primary-source/research qualification; semantic agreement with this private book does not license copying it or close provenance debt.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled imperfective/perfective timing prose; complete formation exceptions, literary passage and recipe NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Active participles, register and short adjectives are in the expected lesson. The app now tests form class, agreement and predicate/attributive function rather than glosses alone, and the time-label reversal is removed. The book labels its punctuation section extra; the authority's required punctuation scope remains a separate governing decision. Neither the private reading nor this audit activates a variance.
lessonAssessments.scope: Section spine, visual short-adjective page and sampled punctuation/short-adjective prose; all active-formation/stress details and native punctuation applications NOT_VERIFIED.

lessonAssessments.conclusion: Letter names, abbreviations and particles fit the final lesson. New checks ask for Russian names and initialism interpretation, replacing source-table position recall. The app uses a different admitted capstone story from the book; that can be independent practice, but equivalence to the book's whole-story integration is not established.
lessonAssessments.scope: Headings and sampled dictionary/abbreviation/particle prose; full Chekhov text, every particle use and capstone-equivalence comparison NOT_VERIFIED.
